### Abnormal T cell subset number `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025540`
#### Removed
- [Abnormal T cell subset number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025540) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Abnormal increase or decrease of any T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group." 

- [Abnormal T cell subset number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025540) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Abnormal T cell subset distribution" 

#### Added
- [Abnormal T cell subset number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025540) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes) of any T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group." 

- [Abnormal T cell subset number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025540) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Absolute counts (cells per microliter) and proportions (percentage of lymphocytes or of a parent subset) capture different information, so clinical practice uses whichever is validated for a given decision. Some thresholds are count-based (e.g. Pneumocystis prophylaxis in adults); others rest on a proportion or on both, as in the SCID definition, which combines an absolute T-cell count with a naive-CD4 proportion. The choice is also age-dependent, since absolute counts vary with age more than percentages do, so percentages are often preferred in young children. Because a count equals a proportion multiplied by the total lymphocyte number, the two can dissociate: a normal proportion may accompany a low absolute count when total lymphocytes are low, and that dissociation can itself be informative." 

- [Abnormal T cell subset number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025540) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Abnormal T cell subset number" 


### Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020317`

#### Added
- Class: [Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020317) 

- [Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020317) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "The abdominal aorta extends from the T12 vertebra and terminates at the L4 vertebra. It gives off anterior, lateral, and posterior branches that supply the abdominal viscera and vertebrae at this level, eventually dividing into the common iliac arteries. Upaired branches (and their typical location) comprise the celiac artery (T12), the superior mesenteric artery (L1), the inferior mesenteric artery (L3), and the median sacral artery. Paired branches comprise the middle adrenal arteries, the renal arteries (L1-2), the gonadal arteries (between L2 and L3), the inferior phrenic arteries, and the lumbar arteries. The abdominal aorta bifurcates into right and left common iliac arteries at L4." 

- [Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020317) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology" 

- [Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020317) SubClassOf [Abnormal systemic arterial morphology](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0011004)

- [Abnormal circulating fetuin-A concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033305) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Any deviation from the normal concentration of fetuin-A in the blood circulation." 

- [Abnormal circulating fetuin-A concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033305) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Fetuin-A (FetA) is a 64-kDa glycoprotein that is found in relatively high concentrations in human serum. In human adults, FetA is mainly expressed and secreted from the liver and adipose tissue. Epidemiologic research consistently observes elevated circulating FetA in obesity and related complications, such as type 2 diabetes mellitus, the metabolic syndrome, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease."

### Abnormal circulating globulin concentration `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032179`

#### Added
- Class: [Abnormal circulating globulin concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032179) 

- [Abnormal circulating globulin concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032179) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Any deviation from the normal concentration of globulins in the blood circulation." 

- [Abnormal circulating globulin concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032179) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Albumin makes up more than half of the total protein present in serum. The remaining blood proteins except albumin and fibrinogen (which is not in serum) are referred to as globulins. The globulin fraction includes hundreds of serum proteins including carrier proteins, enzymes, complement, and immunoglobulins. Most of these are synthesized in the liver, although the immunoglobulins are synthesized by plasma cells. Globulins are divided into four groups by electrophoresis. The four fractions are alpha1, alpha2, beta and gamma, depending on their migratory pattern between the anode and the cathode." 

- [Abnormal circulating globulin concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032179) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Abnormal circulating globulin concentration" 

- [Abnormal circulating globulin concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032179) SubClassOf [Abnormal circulating protein concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0010876)

- [Abnormal circulating monosaccharide concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020347) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "The simplest carbohydrates are called monosaccharides, or simple sugars. They are the building blocks (monomers) for the synthesis of polymers or complex carbohydrates. Monosaccharides are classified based on the number of carbons in the molecule. General categories are identified using a prefix that indicates the number of carbons and the suffix -ose, which indicates a saccharide; for example, triose (three carbons), tetrose (four carbons), pentose (five carbons), and hexose (six carbons). The hexose D-glucose is the most abundant monosaccharide in nature."

### Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025183`
#### Removed
- [Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025183) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Abnormal increase or decrease of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population." 

- [Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025183) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Abnormal CD4+ T cell proportion" 

#### Added
- [Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025183) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population." 

- [Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025183) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Absolute counts (cells per microliter) and proportions (percentage of lymphocytes or of a parent subset) capture different information, so clinical practice uses whichever is validated for a given decision. Some thresholds are count-based (e.g. Pneumocystis prophylaxis in adults); others rest on a proportion or on both, as in the SCID definition, which combines an absolute T-cell count with a naive-CD4 proportion. The choice is also age-dependent, since absolute counts vary with age more than percentages do, so percentages are often preferred in young children. Because a count equals a proportion multiplied by the total lymphocyte number, the two can dissociate: a normal proportion may accompany a low absolute count when total lymphocytes are low, and that dissociation can itself be informative." 

- [Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0025183) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number"

It is mostly produced by the liver, up-regulated by estrogens, and suppressed by steroids. Clinically, high levels are observed in pregnancy. Low levels may be observed in patients with cirrhosis as well as with corticosteroid-binding globulin deficiency caused by variants in CBG (MIM:611489)."

### Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032233`

#### Added
- Class: [Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032233) 

- [Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032233) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "The concentration of creatine kinase BB isoform in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal." 

- [Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032233) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "All CK isoforms are encoded by separate nuclear genes and, in most tissues, a single cytosolic CK isoform is co-expressed together with a single mitochondrial CK isoform (mtCK). Cytosolic muscle-type CK (M-CK) and brain-type CK (B-CK) form homodimers or heterodimers, e.g. MM-CK in skeletal muscle, MM, MB and BB-CK in heart, or BB-CK in brain, kidney, spermatozoa, skin and many other tissues. MtCK is situated in the outer mitochondrial compartment and occurs as sarcomeric mtCK (smtCK) expressed mainly in muscle tissue and as ubiquitous mtCK (umtCK) expressed in a large number of other cells and tissues. CK-MB levels can rise upon myocardial injury, CK-MM rises upon skeletal muscle damage, and CK-BB can rise with brain injury." 

- [Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032233) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration"

([increased amount](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000470) and ([characteristic of](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000052) some 
([creatine kinase B-type (human)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PR_P12277) and ([part of](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_0000050) some [blood](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_0000178)))) and ([has modifier](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002573) some [abnormal](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000460)))

### Unusual CNS infection `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0011450`
#### Removed
- [Unusual CNS infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0011450) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "A type of infection of the central nervous system that can be regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection." 

#### Added
- [Unusual CNS infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0011450) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Increased susceptibility to infections of the central nervous system, as manifested by recurrent, severe, or invasive infections involving the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. This can include infections caused by opportunistic or atypical pathogens, or common pathogens presenting with unusual severity or in anatomical locations." 


### Unusual infection `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032101`

#### Added
- [Unusual infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032101) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Increased susceptibility to infection, as manifested by recurrent infection, severe or invasive infection, infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location, or infection with opportunistic organisms, that is unusual for a healthy individual of the same age." 

- [Unusual infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0032101) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "There are five general subtypes. (i) Opportunistic infection, meaning infection by a pathogen that is not normally able to cause infection in a healthy host (e.g., pneumonia by Pneumocystis jirovecii or CMV); (ii) Unusual location (focus) of an infection (e.g., an aspergillus brain abscess); (iii) a protracted course or lack of adequate response to treatment (e.g., chronic rhinosinusitis); (iv) Unusual severity or intensity of an infection; and (v) unusual recurrence of infections." 


### Unusual lower respiratory tract infection `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210123`

- [Unusual lower respiratory tract infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210123) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections, including bronchiectasis, are characteristic of antibody deficiencies and combined immunodeficiencies." 

- [Unusual lower respiratory tract infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210123) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Unusual lower respiratory tract infection"

### Unusual upper respiratory tract infection `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210121`

#### Added
- Class: [Unusual upper respiratory tract infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210121) 

- [Unusual upper respiratory tract infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210121) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Increased susceptibility to infection of the upper respiratory tract, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the nose, sinuses, pharynx, larynx, or middle ear, or by infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism." 

- [Unusual upper respiratory tract infection](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5210121) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Recurrent or severe sinopulmonary infections are characteristic of humoral (B-cell) deficiencies, complement defects, and phagocyte disorders. This phenotype is also frequently observed in combined immunodeficiencies (e.g., DOCK8 deficiency) and hyper-IgE syndromes (e.g., STAT3 deficiency)."

### isoprostane `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_138408`

#### Added
- Class: [isoprostane](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_138408) 

- [isoprostane](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_138408) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "Any icosanoid with a prostaglandin-like structure formed in vivo by non-enzymatic free radical-catalysed reactions involving peroxidation of essential fatty acids (mainly arachidonic acid but also other fatty acids with 3 or more double bonds). Isoprostanes are abundant in tissues and fluids and have immunomodulating activity. Their concentration is dependent on the amount of oxidative stress and may be upregulated in certain diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular and neurological disorders."

- [muscle relaxant](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_51371) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "A drug used to produce muscle relaxation (excepting neuromuscular blocking agents). Its primary clinical and therapeutic use is the treatment of muscle spasm and immobility associated with strains, sprains, and injuries of the back and, to a lesser degree, injuries to the neck. Also used for the treatment of a variety of clinical conditions that have in common only the presence of skeletal muscle hyperactivity, for example, the muscle spasms that can occur in multiple sclerosis."
